source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Advanced Accessor expiry_date meta field
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new mechanism: passing an `expiry_date` field inside the meta object of an Advanced Accessor call (e.g. `couchbase.replace(src_col,{"id":meta.id,"expiry_date":expiryDate},doc)`) to set a document's TTL directly, in place of N1QL()

concepts.label: Bucket Max Time-to-Live (hard expiration ceiling)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing candidate found in registry slice; a bucket-level constraint enforced server-side across all mutation paths (SQL++, Eventing, SDK), not specific to any one of them

concepts.label: N1QL() function call from within an Eventing handler
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - distinct from js-udf:n1ql-function-call (a different product surface, JavaScript UDFs); needed only as the comparison object for the mustUseInsteadWhen relation below

relations.subject: eventing:accessor-expiry-date-field
relations.evidence: You can improve your function's performance by avoiding N1QL() and using `couchbase.replace(bucket_binding, meta, doc)` instead.

relations.subject: capella:bucket-max-ttl
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures a server-side ceiling override on a document property regardless of mutation path
relations.evidence: If a `Bucket Max Time-to-Live` is set and specified in seconds, it's enforced as a hard upper limit. Any subsequent document mutation, whether by SQL++, Eventing, or a Couchbase SDK, results in the document having its expiration adjusted and set to the bucket's maximum TTL if the operation has: No TTL / A TTL of zero / A TTL greater than the bucket's TTL

relations.subject: eventing:accessor-expiry-date-field
relations.evidence: There are two variants of this function available: a [Couchbase Server version 6.6 that relies on SQL++](eventing-handler-docControlledSelfExpiry.md), and a Couchbase Server version 6.6.1+/7.0.0+ that directly sets the expiration.

notable_absence.finding: Server-version-string citations recur here ('Couchbase Server version 6.6', 'version 6.6.1+/7.0.0+', plus the usual 'Version 7.1+/7.0+/6.6.1' code-comment ladder) - flagged as recurrence of the known anomaly, not treated as new. No Enterprise/Community edition badge appears on this page.

cross_component_finding: The Bucket Max TTL enforcement rule is stated as applying identically 'whether by SQL++, Eventing, or a Couchbase SDK' - a cross-component constraint that lives at the bucket/KV layer, not an Eventing-specific behavior, even though this page is the one demonstrating it via Eventing.
